_comment: The known-open fleet defect floor, as a COMMITTED artifact rather than a Python literal.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (T-167, 2026-08-17). The ratchet assertions in
test_fleet_script_health.py can only run where the real fleet bus exists — on CI they
pytest.skip(). So a PR that empties the floor is validated by a CI run that CANNOT SEE the
fleet, and 'all green' means only 'the assertions did not run'. That is exactly what
happened: commit a5cde31 (2026-08-12) emptied the floor claiming 'all six T-071 findings
fixed', CI passed, and on 2026-08-17 all six still reproduced verbatim — plus a NEW
keeper-tick.cmd finding that had been invisible for five days. The gate detected the
defects and its own bookkeeping threw the signal away: the detect-then-discard class this
checker exists to catch, one level up, inside the checker.
THE CONTRACT. Every entry records the run that OBSERVED it. Shrinking the floor is a
claim about the live fleet, so it must carry evidence a reviewer can re-derive:
1. run the checker on the fleet host (see reproduce_with below),
2. remove only entries that genuinely stopped reproducing,
3. update observed_on to that run's date.
test_known_open_fleet_findings_still_reproduce enforces the floor is real ON THE HOST. On
CI, where the fleet is absent, test_ratchet_floor_is_evidenced still runs and blocks a
floor edit whose observed_on was not refreshed — so an unevidenced shrink can no longer
merge green.
RULE: entries may only be REMOVED (as the fleet lands fixes), never added to excuse a new
defect. A new defect is a red test, not a new line here.
ZERO-FLOOR CONTRACT (T-212, 2026-08-19). findings CAN be empty — that is the success
condition the whole sweep exists to reach — but ONLY together with a zero_evidence block.
A prose claim ('all fixed, trust me') costs nothing to write, so it is explicitly REJECTED
(test_floor_guard_rejects_empty_floor_without_evidence replays a5cde31 exactly). What
zero_evidence carries instead is manifest_sha256: a sha256 over every scanned fleet
script's (relative path, content sha256), sorted — computed by
check_fleet_script_health.manifest_digest() / `--print-zero-evidence`. Producing a digest
that matches the live fleet requires actually reading the live fleet's real files; nobody
can hand-type a sha256 that happens to match dozens of real files' real content. On any
host that DOES have the fleet, test_zero_floor_evidence_matches_live_fleet recomputes this
digest and fails loudly the moment it drifts from what is committed here — whether the
drift is honest (the fleet changed) or fabricated (the evidence was never actually run).
That is the same host-gated-truth pattern that already governs a non-empty floor
(test_known_open_fleet_findings_still_reproduce), extended to cover the zero case, which
the pre-T-212 shape of this file could not express at all.

T-320 (2026-08-26) REPOPULATED a floor that had legitimately reached zero. This is NOT the forbidden "add a line to excuse a new defect": the four entries below were INVISIBLE to the checker on 2026-08-19 because no check for their classes existed yet. T-320 built four new gates (unmeasured-reset, dead-convention-guard, clobbered-exit, unchecked-chdir), each with self-tests that fail when the check is stubbed to return [], and each then fired on the LIVE fleet. The defects are in the GetWorkDone fleet repo, not in this hub repo, so this hub PR cannot fix them - it can only make them visible and hold the line. The zero_evidence block from 2026-08-19 was REMOVED because it is now factually false: the fleet does carry known silent-failure defects. Shrinking this floor still requires the same evidence contract as before.
observed_by: T-320 (fleet-script adversarial audit, week 3). Ran the checker against the live bus at C:/Abhay/GetWorkDone with the four new T-320 gates wired in; all four entries below reproduced. Each was independently verified at source before being gated - bus-sync.sh data loss was reproduced end-to-end (evidence/2026-08-26-T-320/repro-bus-sync-dataloss.sh), and the cd /d semantics were reproduced on a real cmd.exe.
reproduce_with: PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/check_fleet_script_health.py <fleet-dir> --caller .claude/skills/get-work-done/SKILL.md   (fleet-dir = D:/Abhay/GetWorkDone on the dev PC, C:/Abhay/GetWorkDone on the Windows VPS; scripts/tests/test_fleet_script_health.py's _resolve_fleet_dir() resolves this automatically). Add --print-zero-evidence to regenerate the zero_evidence block below.

removal_evidence.keeper-tick.cmd/silent-staging: Never a genuine defect at this site: T-207 guards every git mutation before the push by asserting on OUTPUT CONTENT captured into a per-tick temp file (findstr/for-of into a flag variable, then an `if` on that flag), then KT_ABORT and a goto before the push — that file is forbidden from using `if errorlevel` there because its own header records six failed fixes proving errorlevel is unreliable after a redirect into a shared log. T-210 taught check_silent_staging (CONTENT_ASSERTION_READ/CONTENT_ASSERTION_GATE) to recognise this content-assertion shape as an equally valid verdict read, so it no longer false-positives on it.
removal_evidence.worker-wrapper.ps1/unchecked-preconditio: Genuinely fixed by T-211 commit 16e1316: worker-wrapper.ps1 now tests $LASTEXITCODE right after invoking trust-workspace.py and aborts the launch (exit 9, no result.json written) on a non-zero exit. Re-proved by the supervisor: a stub trust-workspace.py exiting 3 gives the wrapper exit 9 and no worker is ever started.

open_finding_notes.bus-sync.sh/unmeasured-reset: bus-sync.sh:8 - bus_pull() reads the EMPTY output of a failed `git log @{u}..HEAD` (exit 128, unresolvable upstream) as "no unpushed commits to lose" and hard-resets over them, returning 0. Reproduced end-to-end; the commit is destroyed and the fleet records a healthy tick. Fix belongs in the GetWorkDone repo: resolve the upstream fail-closed before the probe.
open_finding_notes.keeper-tick.cmd/unchecked-chdir: keeper-tick.cmd:26, :212, :256 - a failed `cd /d` sets errorlevel 1, does NOT abort, and leaves cwd UNCHANGED, so the git add/commit/push below run against the previous repository. :212 is the one hardcoded absolute path never migrated to %~dp0. Fix: `if errorlevel 1 ( alert & exit /b 1 )` immediately after each chdir.
open_finding_notes.worker-wrapper.ps1/clobbered-exit: worker-wrapper.ps1:755 - `git add -A`'s exit code is overwritten by `git commit` before the $LASTEXITCODE test reads it, so a partial staging failure is reported to the dispatcher as a successful autosave to a rescue branch. Fix: capture `$addRc = $LASTEXITCODE` before the commit runs.
